title: Ideal-power quotient of a coherent formal-module limit sheaf
statement: Let $Y$ be a Noetherian scheme, $J$ a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf, $G$ a coherent $J$-adic formal module [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], and $n\in\mathbb N$. Write $L=\varprojlim G$ for its limit in $\mathcal O_Y$-module sheaves. There is an isomorphism $e:L/J^{n+1}L\simeq G_n$ such that the quotient projection followed by $e$ equals the canonical limit projection $L\to G_n$. The indexing convention labels level $n+1$ by $n$.

source.place: Lemma 087W, formula M/I^n M=M_n; local uniqueness in first half of Lemma 088B. Sources read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/087W and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/088B.

proof.text: For each affine open V, transport coherentFormalModule_affine_projections through preservesLimitIso for the evaluation functor. The projection on sheaf sections is surjective, and its kernel is J(V)^(n+1) times all sections of the sheaf limit. This transport uses the comparison projection equation and the comap of ideal multiples under a linear isomorphism.

Let p be the level projection, i the inclusion of the ideal-power product into the sheaf limit L, and q its cokernel projection. Apply formalModuleQuotient_factor to p with equal exponents n+1. The product on the target level is zero by the annihilation condition in the coherent formal module definition. Hence i followed by p is zero. This replaces the tensor-stalk argument for this inclusion.

The quotient projection q kills J(V)^(n+1) times L(V). Indeed apply ideal_times_quasiCoherent_affine_sections to the unit sheaf to lift each ideal-power scalar through the power inclusion. Its product with an arbitrary section of L is the image of the corresponding pure tensor section under multiplication. Multiplication factors through i, so its composite with q is zero. Submodule.smul_le extends this to all ideal multiples. The affine kernel formula then shows kernel.ι p followed by q vanishes on every affine open, hence globally by applying the faithful SheafOfModules.toSheaf functor and the existing Mathlib TopCat.Sheaf.hom_ext theorem on the affine basis. No duplicate affine-separatedness helper is introduced. No quasi-coherence of L or preservation of sheaf images by evaluation is assumed.

Affine surjectivity implies p is locally surjective and therefore epi. Construct a from the formal quotient to the level using cokernel.desc i p, and b in the other direction by Abelian.epiDesc p q since kernel.ι p followed by q is zero. The equations q followed by a equals p and p followed by b equals q show a and b are inverse by cancelling the epimorphisms q and p. Their isomorphism satisfies exactly the required projection equation. All arguments include empty schemes and J=0 or J=1.

lean.statement:
theorem coherentFormalModule_limit_quotient {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian Y]
    (J : Y.IdealSheafData) (G : CoherentFormalModule Y J) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ e : formalModuleQuotient J (n + 1) (limit G.obj) ≅ G.obj.obj (op n),
      formalModuleQuotientπ J (n + 1) (limit G.obj) ≫ e.hom =
        limit.π G.obj (op n)
